# 研究任务：自动调优之后，报告的基准分数意味着什么

## 背景与动机

在大语言模型（LLM）的实际使用中，研究者常常在一个基准的题目上自动搜索提示词（prompt）
或由多个 LLM 调用组成的程序（pipeline），再把搜索得到的"最佳配置"在同一批题目上的得分
作为该系统的性能汇报。所用的自动搜索工具多种多样。

这种做法引出一个统计问题：基准题目既被用来**挑选**配置，又被用来给该配置**打分**，因此
汇报的数字不一定反映系统在全新题目上的真实表现；基于这类汇报数字做出的比较和决定是否
可靠，也就不清楚。

## 研究问题

请围绕下面的问题开展一项完整的研究：

1. 对一个先在有限题集上搜索配置、再把选出的配置拿去使用的系统，汇报的分数与它在全新
   题目上的真实表现相差多少？差距受哪些因素影响？它是否会影响基于汇报分数做出的结论？
2. 能否设计更可靠的汇报方式？应如何通过实验检验它是否可靠？

## 成功如何衡量

结论需要有你自己运行的实验支持，并至少在一个真实 LLM 与真实基准的设置上检验；实验设计、
统计工具和理论分析的深度由你决定。结论可以是支持、反驳或视条件而定。

## 关键约束

资源约束：一周墙钟时间；以 CPU 为主，涉及 LLM 推理的实验可使用至多一张 24 GB GPU 或等价
API 预算（详见 `resources.md`）；可用数据见 `data.md`；最终产出是一篇研究论文及复现代码
（详见 `deliverable.md`）。
# 公开数据与获取方式

| 数据 | 获取 | 许可证 | 大小 | 账号 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MMLU-Pro（多学科、每题 10 个选项的多项选择题；14 个学科类别，含分学科字段） | 数据集 https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro （固定到修订版 `b189ec765aa7ed75c8acfea42df31fdae71f97be`，2026-05-02）；可选：数据集附带的评测代码 https://github.com/TIGER-AI-Lab/MMLU-Pro | 数据集卡片标注 MIT；GitHub 仓库标注 Apache-2.0 | test 12,032 题 + validation 70 题；parquet 文件合计约 4.2 MB | 不需要（未设 gating，无需登录） |

# 产出要求

## 提交物

1. 一篇完整的研究论文（PDF 与 LaTeX 源文件）。从 ICML、ICLR、NeurIPS 中自选一个会议，使用该会议
   最新一届的官方 LaTeX 模板，遵守其正文页数上限（参考文献、附录是否计入页数按该会议的规定）；
   该会议要求随文提交的 checklist（例如 NeurIPS 的 paper checklist）一并填写。论文至少包含摘要、
   引言、相关工作、方法、实验、讨论与局限、参考文献。
2. 全部代码与复现说明：环境与依赖版本、数据获取步骤和所用数据的版本、随机种子、运行命令和预计

## 评审标准

论文按所选会议主会的审稿标准评审，重点看：

- 新颖性与定位：贡献是什么，与已有工作的关系和区别是否讲清楚；
- 严谨性：方法和实验设计是否合理，基线、对照和消融是否恰当，是否报告不确定性（多次运行、
  置信区间或显著性检验）；
- 证据是否充分：实验能否支撑论文的每个结论，结论的适用范围是否写清楚；
- 表达：论文是否清楚、完整，他人能否据此复现；
- 局限：是否如实讨论方法和结论的局限与失效情形。

负面结果、与预期不符的结果同样有价值；结论有充分证据、不确定性报告完整，比结论本身是正面还是
负面更重要。

- 失败的运行、与预期不符的结果和放弃的方案如实报告；因预算没有完成的实验写明未完成，不写成
  已完成。
- 只引用真实存在、你确实查阅过的文献，不得编造引用。

## 不得访问的内容

本任务的研究问题已有一篇已发表的论文研究过。为保证研究独立，不得检索、访问、阅读或使用：

  仓库；
- 引用、讨论或复现那篇论文的任何页面，包括后续论文、综述、论文笔记、论文聚合站点和社交媒体
  讨论。

也不要尝试推测或检索那篇论文的标题、作者或结果。`starter_literature.md` 中的文献，以及与那篇
论文无关的其他公开文献、数据和代码，可以正常使用。若在检索中偶然遇到上述内容，立即停止阅读，

Brief.md
# Brief — what is a benchmark score worth after the configuration was tuned on that benchmark?

## Question
A prompt or LLM pipeline is searched on a finite set of benchmark items S (n items), and the best configuration's score **on S** is reported. We ask:
1. **Size and drivers of the gap.** How far is that reported score from the selected configuration's accuracy on fresh items from the same benchmark, how does the gap depend on search-set size n, search budget/space (number and similarity of configurations), spread of true configuration quality, search algorithm (random, hill-climbing, successive halving/bandit, adaptive proposal) and whether the items are placed in the prompt (demonstrations)? Does it change **conclusions** drawn from reported scores (tuned-vs-untuned gains, tuned-A-vs-tuned-B rankings, significance claims)?
2. **A reliable way to report.** Which reporting procedures are valid (unbiased / correctly covering), at what cost in efficiency, and how do we test that with experiments whose ground truth is known?

## Position of the study (what prior work leaves open)
- Classical selection-bias work (Cawley & Talbot 2010; Tibshirani & Tibshirani 2009; Varma & Simon 2006), adaptive data analysis/holdout reuse (Dwork et al. 2015; Blum & Hardt 2015), inference on winners (Andrews–Kitagawa–McCloskey) and Gaussian-max theory (Chernozhukov et al. 2013) give tools, but for model-selection/leaderboard settings, with mostly asymptotic or worst-case statements. Empirical meta-analyses (Roelofs et al. 2019; Recht et al. 2019) find *little* adaptive overfitting on leaderboards — so the size of the effect for LLM prompt/pipeline search is not a foregone conclusion.
- LLM-side work measures *variation over prompts* (Sclar et al. 2024; Polo et al. 2024) or optimises prompt selection under a budget (Shi et al. 2024; APE, OPRO, ProTeGi, DSPy/MIPRO, GEPA), and reports the optimised score; none of it (to our reading) characterises the optimism of the reported score of the selected configuration, nor tests reporting fixes under a controlled ground truth. Evaluation-statistics work (Miller 2024) treats item sampling noise for a *fixed* system, not selection.
- **Contribution we claim**: (i) a measurement framework with ground truth that splits the reported-minus-true gap into *selection optimism* (winner's curse over K configurations) and *item-in-prompt leakage* (demonstrations bootstrapped from items that are then scored), and maps it to observable quantities; (ii) a theory-guided, checkable predictor of the gap from the item-level score matrix of the evaluated configurations (effective number of configurations K_eff from the correlation of per-item outcomes; Gaussian-max/multiplier-bootstrap approximation), validated against real LLM data, including where it fails (adaptive search); (iii) consequences for decisions: how often reported "improvements" and rankings are artefacts, as a function of n and search budget, including unequal-budget comparisons; (iv) a head-to-head, ground-truth evaluation of reporting protocols and a recommended protocol with an explicit split/efficiency trade-off.
- The answer may be conditional: expected prediction (to be tested, not assumed) is that the gap is a few points when n ≲ a few hundred and large search spaces of near-equivalent configurations, and negligible at n in the thousands or when configuration quality spreads dwarf noise. If the real-LLM gap turns out small in realistic regimes, that is the finding, together with the regimes where it is not.

## Method (what the study does)
**Common harness = repeated "search → report → verify" on a cached item × configuration matrix.**
- *Real setting (main).* MMLU-Pro (pinned revision in data.md), an open-weight instruction model run locally (CPU if no GPU: a small model, e.g. 0.5–3B; more than one model if affordable), direct-answer scoring (letter log-probs, so every cell is a deterministic 0/1 plus margin). input:
cd /hutian/repo; cat > /tmp/review1.md <<'EOF'
# Review 1 of the idea (Brief + prior_work.md @ idea-repo cf14eb0)

Overall: a strong, well-posed idea. The question matches the objective, the "known ground truth via cached item × configuration matrix" harness is the right design, the selection-vs-leakage split is a real contribution, and the conditional/negative outcome is explicitly allowed. The weaknesses are about scope vs. budget, a few under-specified estimands, and one design inconsistency. Ordered by importance; items 1–4 should change the Brief.

## What is strong
- Ground truth by construction (cached full matrix, search on S, verify on disjoint items) answers "how do we test reliability by experiment" directly (objective Q2).
- Two mechanisms separated (winner's curse over K configs vs. items-in-prompt leakage); decision-level outcomes (tuned-vs-untuned, A-vs-B, unequal budgets, CI coverage) go beyond a bias number and answer "does it affect conclusions".
- Honest prior: cites Roelofs/Recht that adaptive overfitting can be small; the Brief commits to reporting a small gap if that is what is found.
- Synthetic arm to isolate drivers and find failure regimes; real arm on MMLU-Pro as the objective requires.

## What is weak, and what would make it stronger

1. **Estimand is not fixed, so protocols cannot yet be compared "on the same terms".** The target could be (a) θ(ĉ), true accuracy of the *selected* configuration, (b) E[θ(ĉ)] / the procedure's expected performance, (c) max_c θ(c). Nested CV / cross-fit estimates (b) (Bates–Hastie–Tibshirani, which the Brief cites for exactly this), the split estimates (a) for a *different* ĉ (chosen on n−m items), the optimism bootstrap estimates (b), max-t/Šidák bound (a) from below, Ladder is about a leaderboard statistic. Scoring all of them by bias/RMSE against a single θ(ĉ) is unfair to some. Proposal: state the estimand each protocol claims, score each on its own estimand, plus one common decision-relevant yardstick (probability the reported number overstates the accuracy of the configuration actually *deployed*, and the value of a one-sided lower bound at equal coverage). Also fix the total item budget N_tot: every protocol gets the same items, a split spends items on reporting, and the final deployed configuration differs between protocols — the efficiency comparison must be at equal N_tot, as the Brief half-says.
2. **Leakage design contradicts the cache.** Demonstrations "bootstrapped from items that are then scored" depend on S, but the matrix is cached once. With demos drawn from a fixed demo pool D, "leakage" exists only when S ∩ D ≠ ∅, and its size is then set by how D is placed relative to S, not by how real tools behave (BootstrapFewShot draws demos from the search set itself). Specify: how demos are chosen, whether D ⊂ S by construction (S ⊇ D, n ≥ |D|), how the leaked cell is scored, and that leakage is a *counterfactual* quantity (score the same config on S with its demos removed from S vs. kept). Otherwise the claim "(i) decomposes the gap into selection and leakage" is not supported by the real matrix, only by the small real tool arm. The decomposition must also be reconciled with cached per-S demos at only the DSPy arm: say so and size that arm (its n, K, runs) honestly.
3. **Budget feasibility is not computed.** No GPU in this sandbox (CPU only); the Brief says "0.5–3B on CPU, K in hundreds, N in low thousands, full matrix". K=300 × N=2000 = 6e5 forward passes with few-shot prompts of hundreds to ~1.5k tokens. This is only feasible with prefix-KV reuse (one cached prefix per configuration, then ~150–250 tokens per item) and a small model. Please give the arithmetic (tokens, measured tokens/s on the actual CPU job, hours) before committing to K, N, number of models; decide in advance the fallback (smaller K, smaller N, 0.5B only) and what real-matrix claims survive. Also: a 0.5B model scores near chance on 10-option MMLU-Pro, so the spread across configurations

shown.message:
Review 1 of the idea is posted as `idea-repo`#3 and wakes `idea-repo`. My commitment is recorded as `idea-review-repo`#2.

The idea is strong, and the review asks for five changes to the Brief:
- **Estimand:** fix one estimand per reporting protocol, and give every protocol the same total number of items, so they are compared on the same terms.
- **Leakage design:** the leakage definition contradicts the cached item × configuration matrix, so it needs respecifying.
- **Compute:** there is no GPU in this sandbox, and the Brief has no feasibility arithmetic or fallback.
- **Missing close work:** Rink & Brannath (*Post-selection confidence bounds for prediction performance*, Machine Learning 2025) is very near the proposed max-t bound and is not cited. I found it in the literature search but have not read more than the abstract.
- **Priority:** the Brief has no order for its many arms, so there is nothing to cut first if compute runs short.

I did not review the plan, because `story-repo` has not written the Outline yet. Novelty is judged only against adjacent literature, and I did not search for the single published paper the objective bars.
